Build the IPCC 2019 wet/dry drivers of the nitrogen loss cascade.

Source: R/n_loss_drivers.R
build_n_loss_drivers.Rd

Put the IPCC 2019 Tier 1 wet/dry class of build_cell_moisture_regime(), and the Atlantic/Mediterranean drivers mapped from it, on every row of a gridded nitrogen balance, as the two driver tables build_nitrogen_balance() joins: n_balance_drivers (per balance key and loss fert_type, read by calculate_nh3(), calculate_soil_n2o() and calculate_indirect_n2o_nh3()) and n_balance_leaching_drivers (per balance key, read by calculate_n_leaching()). build_nitrogen_balance() calls it itself at grid resolution when neither table is supplied.

A row whose cell, polity, commodity balance item and water regime has a class of its own takes it. A row without one takes its cell's class on precipitation alone (no crop, no irrigation): a row with no crop item, as the soil organic matter sequestration rows, and a row of an item WHEP holds no land of in that water regime, as grass. A cell lacking CRU climate variables takes them from its nearest CRU land cell (see build_cell_moisture_regime()). Every row ends with a class.

climate is "ATL" on wet rows and "MED" on dry rows. irrig_type, the n2o_efs_disaggregated key of the Atlantic/Mediterranean options, is "Flooded" on every rice row (the commodity balance item of the production items classed Crop_irrig == "Rice" in items_prod_full) in both climates and both water regimes, "Med_average" on other irrigated MED rows, "Rainfed" on other rainfed MED rows and "Tier_1" on every other ATL row (the ATL table defines only "Tier_1" and "Flooded").

Usage

build_n_loss_drivers(
  rows = NULL,
  window = c("trailing_30", "annual", "normal"),
  water = c("precip_irrig", "precip"),
  data = NULL,
  config = list(),
  example = FALSE
)

Source

IPCC (2019), 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 4, Chapter 11, Table 11.1, footnote 4 (p. 11.13).

Arguments

rows

The balance rows to give drivers: lon, lat, area_code, item_cbs_code (NA on rows without a crop), year and water_regime ("rainfed" or "irrigated"), plus optionally fert_type, the loss fert_type of each row. With fert_type, the loss drivers are built for its non-missing (key, fert_type) pairs; without it, for every key and the seven loss fert_types ("Excreta", "Liquid", "Solid", "SOM", "Synthetic", "Human", "Recycling"). The leaching drivers cover every key. n_input_t, the N of each row, is needed wherever an irrigated row has no class of its own: such a row must carry no N.

window, water, config

As in build_cell_moisture_regime(). The window also sets the precipitation-only class of rows without a crop.

data

Optional list of inputs, passed to build_cell_moisture_regime() (climate, crop_depth, lpjml_years, lpjml_grid, regime_areas, country_grid), plus moisture_regime, a build_cell_moisture_regime() result to use instead of building it. Climate is read once and shared.

example

If TRUE, return a small fixture instead of reading data. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A named list of two tibbles:

  • n_balance_drivers: one row per balance key (lon, lat, area_code, item_cbs_code, year, water_regime) and fert_type, with moisture_regime ("wet" or "dry"), climate ("ATL" or "MED"), irrig_type, method_moisture_regime, method_climate ("from_moisture_regime") and climate_fill_km.

  • n_balance_leaching_drivers: one row per balance key, with moisture_regime, method_moisture_regime and climate_fill_km.

Both are join tables keyed on the balance key; the balance they are joined to carries the polity columns.

Details

Which driver columns each loss method reads, and which this function supplies:

MethodDriver columnsSupplied
nh3: "ipcc"fert_typeyes
nh3: "manner", "manner_default"MANNER's, see belowno
n2o: "ipcc2019"moisture_regimeyes
n2o: "ipcc2019_atl_med"climateyes
n2o: "aguilera", "ipcc2006"climate, irrig_typeyes
n2o_indirect: "ipcc2019"moisture_regimeyes
n2o_indirect: "ipcc2019_atl_med"climate, irrig_typeyes
leaching: "ipcc_fracleach"moisture_regime, water_regimeyes
leaching: "meisinger_drainage"Meisinger's, see belowno

The two methods it does not supply are later work. MANNER reads manner_fertiliser, soil_ph, rate_kg_ha, rainfall_mm, irrigated, temp_c, temp_c_annual_mean, windspeed_ms, technique, system, incorporation_delay_h and species (see calculate_nh3()); Meisinger reads fert_type, climate, irrig_cat, land_use, cn_input, tillage, som_share and drainage_mm (see calculate_n_leaching()). build_nitrogen_balance() refuses either before assembling any input unless its driver table is supplied.

method_moisture_regime is build_cell_moisture_regime()'s stamp. A row that took its cell's precipitation-only class carries the extra field cell_rainfed_class=no_crop_item (no crop item) or cell_rainfed_class=no_regime_area (an item without regime land of the row's water regime), and a row in a cell that took climate variables from its nearest CRU cell the field nearest_cru_cell=<col>[+<col>...], naming them.

Errors

  • whep_n_loss_drivers_rows: rows is missing, empty, lacks a key column, or holds a missing coordinate or year, or a water_regime other than "rainfed" or "irrigated".

  • whep_n_loss_drivers_unclassified: a row is still without a class (for example a window-mean PET of zero), named by its stamp.

  • whep_n_loss_drivers_irrigated_cell_class: an irrigated row carrying N, or one whose N is not supplied, has no class of its own and would take its cell's precipitation-only class. The rainfed/irrigated split gives an irrigated row N only where the item holds irrigated land, so such a row means the balance and the moisture regime disagree on the item's regime land; the error names the count and the items carrying most N.

  • Every error of build_cell_moisture_regime(), including whep_absent_input for an absent climate or irrigation layer.

build_n_loss_drivers(example = TRUE)
